title: Replace a faucet's cartridge so hot stays on the left
instruction: The faucet handle is stiff and won't open fully. Check it, then replace the cartridge with the new one, set so that once the handle is refitted, hot is on the left. Make sure the faucet works before you leave it off, and put the old one in the parts tray.
context: Core plumbing repair. General maintenance and repair workers (1,529,700 jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025) carry the O*NET Core task "Assemble, install, or repair ... pipe systems, plumbing" (49-9071.00); BLS: they "work on plumbing" and "begin by doing simple tasks, such as fixing leaky faucets". Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (465,840; 47-2152.00) "Maintain or repair plumbing". Moen's FAQs give grease or "replace the cartridge" for a stiff 1225; its last step turns the notch forward for hot on the left. The difficulty is in the hands, in a fixed order: feel the old stem's fault; slide a 1.5 mm copper clip out by its tab; pull the cartridge by its 8 mm stem against about 10 N of O-ring drag; push the new one, keyed by its tabs, fully home; thread the clip back through both slots, which it passes only with the cartridge home within about 0.5 mm; turn the stem to within 20 degrees of its set alignment; work the new stem to full-on and both ends without lifting the cartridge; leave it off.
setup: Station table, fixed layout (object_jitter=0); all geometry is built by the task file (no third-party assets); cm, x away from the arms, y to their left, from the midpoint between the arm bases. Fixed: a white solid-surface vanity top 22 x 20 x 1.2 cm centred at x 29, y -10, and on it the faucet with its handle off: a brass valve body, a column 40 mm across and 76 mm tall, axis at x 28, y -12. Its 25 mm bore takes the cartridge; the rim has two 12 mm cut-outs at 12 and 6 o'clock (back and front); two clip slots, 2.5 mm tall and 5 mm wide, run front to back through the wall left and right of the bore, their floor 0.5 mm above the cut-outs' floor; 1.5 mm lead-ins at the rim. Low in the wall, 17 mm above the vanity, a 6 x 6 mm inlet port on each side takes a brass supply shank (8 x 12 x 8 mm) with a 13 mm nut: red (hot) on the left, blue (cold) on the right. A chrome spout (60 x 22 x 16 mm, 21 mm aerator) joins the body just under the clip slots and points at the arms. Behind the faucet lies its chrome lever handle (hub 34 mm across, lever 80 x 14 x 12 mm), red mark on its left, blue on its right: a fixed reference, not refitted. The old cartridge is home in the bore: used grey-tan plastic, body 24 mm across and 65 mm long with two dark inlet windows on its sides, two tabs (8.5 x 8 x 5 mm) on its top shoulder, 40 g; its brass stem, 8 mm across, stands 30 mm above the rim (20 g), down (off). Each stem turns in its cartridge against O-ring drag and lifts toward on. The old stem is stiff: it binds 2 mm up and 15 degrees either way; the new one turns freely and lifts 6 mm to its full-on stop. In each cartridge's top a spring detent ball presses on the stem, holding it where it is left. Inside, as a model of the internals, each stem ends in an 18 mm brass piston with one 6.5 x 6 mm port on the side of the stem's dark notch (2.4 mm wide, 7 mm down its side and across its top). The old notch faces the front. A U-shaped copper retainer clip (legs 52.6 x 4 x 1.5 mm, 19 mm apart; a 10 x 8 mm grab tab standing up at its bight; 7 g) lies in the slots over the cartridge, tab at the front. Fixed on the table: a white PVC holder cup (32 mm across, 20 mm tall) at x 20, y -27 holding the new cartridge upright (white, the same kind, notch to the left), and a grey parts tray, 11 cm square inside with 3 cm walls, at x 33, y -28. Free: both cartridges, both stems, the clip, and each cartridge's 3 mm detent ball (its own body, jointed in the cartridge's top).
scoring: Scored at the end; a full score must hold for 1 s. 0 if the new cartridge, its stem or the clip has at any point left the table (its outline's lowest point 5 cm below the table top, or its centre off the table); 0 while the old cartridge is still in the valve body (its lowest point no more than 2 mm above the rim and its centre within 2.5 cm of the bore's axis). Otherwise 0.25 with the old cartridge out; 0.5 when the new one is home: its body's bottom within 1 mm of where its tabs on the cut-outs' floor put it, its centre within 1.5 mm of the bore's axis, tilted under 3 degrees, tabs within 8 degrees of front-back; 0.75 when, home, it is also clipped and set for hot on the left. Clipped: the clip flat (under 5 degrees), legs within 5 degrees of front-back, its outline reaching at least 11.5 mm past the bore's axis both ways, its lowest point resting on the slots' floor (0.5 mm below to 0.2 mm above it), centred within 2 mm, over a cartridge whose bottom is within 0.5 mm of its seat. Set for hot on the left: Moen's rule, the new stem's notch facing the front (toward the arms) within 20 degrees. The model's piston port sits on the notch's side, so that is the setting where the handle's left swing (modelled as a quarter turn) brings the port onto the hot inlet; the score is that notch rule. A home cartridge that is unclipped, set anywhere else (unturned, reversed or between), or that has risen more than 2 mm under the clip in its slots since it was first clipped (the legs allow 1.5: the 0.5 mm gap under them and their 1 mm of play), stays at 0.5. Each rung counts only when reached in the order a cartridge can be changed in: the old cartridge counts as out only after the clip has been seen out of its way while the old one was still in the valve body, and never if it was forced past the clip; the new one counts as home only if it was seen home with the clip out of its way and wasn't forced past it on the way (once forced, only after standing clear above the slots or off the bore's axis and going home again; and again, after being forced more than 2 mm up its bore with the clip in its way); and clipped only if the clip's latest return into its way found it home. Forced past the clip: seen with the clip over its shoulder (some part of it within 11 mm of the bore's axis in plan: 12 less the cartridge's 0.5 mm side play and 0.5 mm of contact give, so a clip only touching its side doesn't count), its shoulder more than 4 mm above its seat (1 mm past the slots' ceiling; the legs allow 1.5) and its bottom below the slots' top (68 mm), or crossing that span in one step with the clip over its shoulder at either end. Out of its way, read from the clip's own shapes as it lies (not its outline): no part of it within 12 mm (the cartridge's radius) of the bore's axis in plan, however high; for the old cartridge coming out, also lying wholly on or above the rim (at most 0.5 mm into it), or wholly below the slots' floor. 1.0 when also: the faucet was tested before (the old stem lifted at least 1.5 mm up its cartridge in the valve body, before the clip first moved 2 mm from where it was put) and tested after (once the new cartridge has been home and clipped, with its clip retaining it: as clipped, but the legs anywhere in their slots' play, over a cartridge still keyed in the bore and no higher than the legs let it, at most 2 mm; its stem lifted at least 5.5 mm, full-on being 6, and, so lifted, turned so its port faced within 10 degrees of the hot inlet and of the cold inlet, in either order); the faucet is left off (the new stem within 1 mm of its lower stop); the old cartridge lies in the parts tray (centre inside its walls, lowest point under 1.5 cm above its floor); every gripper's tool point and finger pads are at least 1 cm from the new cartridge, its stem and the clip; and those three are still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), held for 1 s. Without either test the job scores 0.75. The old cartridge leaving the table only misses the tray.
reset_notes: Fixed layout. Each reset puts the old cartridge back home with its notch to the front and its stem down, the clip home, and the new cartridge in its holder with its notch to the left and its stem down. Real trial (kit about $450; steps and simple-tool scoring in the README): a new Moen Moentrol 3520 valve body, which takes the 1225 and its copper clip, on its back on the board, inlets unconnected: water off, none at the rig; the score is read dry. Old cartridge: a genuine 1225 with the grease washed out of its stem, reused; at each reset a luggage scale must show it needs at least twice the new one's force to start lifting and turning, and at most 30 N to lift or pull out. Clip edges filed and swab-checked; pads taped. After the trial, any wet check (always before the first trial) is at a separate test station over a dish pan: turn the water on (warm to the left inlet, cold to the right, from funnels), check the left swing runs warmer, and drain and dry before the board returns.
fidelity: Rigid parts at the 1225's approximate size (no drawing published); the valve body is a model (real trial: a Moen Moentrol 3520 body, same 1225 and clip). No water: tests are mechanical; hot and cold follow from the piston's port. O-ring drag: two spring balls (mu about 1.1), about 10 N; a spring ball holds each stem; angular damping on cartridges and stems stands in for twist drag (it damps any spin). The old stem's stiffness is joint limits; the real one drags (README). No seized cartridges.
